ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned advocate Mr. Nishith Thakkar appearing on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. Jay Mehta appearing on behalf of the respondent-State.
2.

The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.
11216022240352 of 2024 registered with the Kalol Taluka Police Station, District Gandhinagar, for the offence punishable under Sections 302, 498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Advocate Mr. Thakkar for the applicant would submit that while the FIR reveals about the incident having taken place on 23.10.2023, yet, the FIR has been registered on 18.05.2024.
Learned NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24817/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined
Advocate would submit that the arrest of the applicant, had taken place even later thereafter i.e. on 21.08.2025.

Learned Advocate would submit that considering the role attributed to the present applicant being mother- in-law of the deceased and having regard to the fact that the co-accused i.e.
sister-in-law having been considered for being released by the learned Sessions Court, this Court may grant regular bail to the present applicant.

Learned Advocate would further submit that the present applicant being a 65 years old lady accused and the charge-sheet having been laid by the Investigating Officer, no fruitful purpose would be served, if the applicant is kept in custody.
Making such submissions, learned Advocate would request this Court to release the present applicant on regular bail.
4. On the other hand, the present application is vehemently objected to by learned APP Mr. Jay Mehta on behalf of the respondent-State.

Learned APP would draw the attention of this Court to the observations made by the learned learned Sessions Court in order dated 15.11.2025 in Criminal Misc. Application No. 468 of 2025, while granting bail to the sister-in-law of the deceased.

Learned APP would submit that in the said order, the learned Sessions Court had gone in detail insofar as the reports by the Forensic Science Laboratory including the report of the Layered Voice Analysis/Scientific Detection of Deception Test etc.

Learned APP NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24817/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined would submit that as such, the present applicant as well as the husband of the deceased were subjected to polygraph test.

It is submitted that the husband of the deceased was also subjected to narco-analysis test and whereas learned APP would submit that from the reports, it would appear that the present applicant was involved in commission of a very heinous crime, more particularly learned APP submitting that the investigation papers as well as the later reports clearly indicating to the fact that the present applicant was the one who had murdered the deceased.
Thus submitting learned APP would request this Court not to consider the present application.

5. Heard learned Advocates for the respective parties and perused the documents including the order passed by the learned Sessions Court, whereby the bail application of the present applicant has been rejected.
6.
This Court having considered the above, is of the opinion that the present is a case where discretion is not required to be exercised in favour of the present applicant for the following reasons.

(i) While it is true that the FIR itself had been registered after a period of approximately seven months, yet, there appears to be clear reason for the FIR to be filed belatedly and whereas it would appear that the applicant has not been prejudiced in any manner whatsoever on account NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24817/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined of the belatedly filing of the FIR.

It would also appear that though the FIR is stated to have been filed belatedly, yet, the material gathered by the Investigating Officer including the reports by the FSL clearly indicate towards the role of the present applicant in the offence in Shardaba Manuji Aluji Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173691780/
2 question.

entities.text: Shardaba Manuji Aluji Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) It would appear in this regard that the FSL had conducted the Layered Voice Analysis/Scientific Detection of Deception Test and as observed by the learned Sessions Court, more particularly not controverted by the present applicant that the deceased appeared to be strangulated to the death by the applicant along with the husband of the deceased.

It would also appear that the polygraph test of the present applicant and the husband of the deceased, revealed that the present applicant with the son of the applicant, during the marriage span of the deceased, used to physically assault the deceased.
(iii) It also appears that the applicant after having done away with the deceased being aware about the said fact, had attended a Navratri Programme.

It would also appear that the husband of the deceased tried to portray as if the the incident was one of a suicide and not a homicide and whereas, the narco-analysis report, clearly appears to have ruled out the same.

7. Considering the above aspects, more particularly having regard to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24817/2025 ORDER DATED: 03/12/2025 undefined the role played by the present applicant of murdering her own daughter- in-law, more particularly the applicant, having harassed and assaulted the daughter-in-law even before committing the crime in question and considering the fact that having done away with the deceased, the applicant had visited a Navratri Programme and whereas also having regard to the fact that the applicant and her son, appear to have deliberately tried to throw the investigation of the track, to this Court it would appear that a prima facie case is made out and furhter considering the gravity of the offence, this would not be a fit case where the discretion granted to this Court is required to be exercised in favour of the present applicant.
Hence, the present application stands disposed of as rejected.
(NIKHIL S. KARIEL,J) BDSONGARA Shardaba Manuji Aluji Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173691780/
